tags.name: La Dieppoise
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-14 -- full wreck-history cross-check per deep-QA policy. Vessel: Bay-class minesweeper, Port Arthur Shipbuilding (Ontario); laid down 8 Jun 1951; launched 21 Jun 1952; commissioned RCN 18 Jun 1954; transferred to France 9 Oct 1954 and renamed La Dieppoise; commissioned French Navy 13 Nov 1954; paid off 9 Jul 1987; scuttled 19 Jan 1988 near Amadee Island (postponed from 12 Jan due to Cyclone Anne). Length 46m/152ft, displacement 390 long tons standard (412 deep load) -- confirmed identically across Wikipedia, newcaledonia-diving.com (official wreck page), and McFadyen; no conflicts on name/build/length/tonnage/cause. Zentacle.com lists an inconsistent sinking date (07/08/1996) that contradicts three corroborating sources and the vessel's own 1987 decommission date -- treated as an unreliable outlier and not used. Corrected stale condition claim: McFadyen's 'basically intact' description dates to 1993; current sources (newcaledonia-diving.com, justgottadive.com) report the wooden hull has since deteriorated/disintegrated while the aluminium frame remains intact -- markdown updated to reflect current condition rather than the 1993 account. Removed unsupported claim that the wreck is 'remarkably intact.' Ship's wheel confirmed still in place (wooden handles eaten away by borers, per McFadyen). Deck depths (flybridge 15m, front deck 18m, rear deck 22m, sand 26m) reconfirmed directly from McFadyen. Sea snakes at this specific wreck confirmed by McFadyen (previously present in markdown without site-specific citation).

tags.name: False Pass
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-14 -- hallucination correction. Went back to McFadyen's actual False Pass page (page_id=508): it states the site 'drops from the surface to 30 metres' and has 'numerous caves, tunnels, holes and bays' -- it does NOT describe a specific '25-metre tunnel exiting at 32 metres' as the prior QA pass's markdown claimed. That specific figure was not found in any source and has been removed as an unconfirmed/likely-fabricated detail; depth corrected from 32m to the sourced 30m. Marine life corrected: turtles and gorgonians are confirmed for this specific site (McFadyen photo captions); tuna, trevally, and grouper were NOT found attributed to this specific site (the marlin/shark-species statistics on McFadyen's page apply to the broader Poum/Pacific Diving operation, not False Pass specifically) and have been removed. Note: there is also an unrelated, well-documented 'Fausse Passe' dive site near Bourail/Ile Verte, ~250km south of this Poum site -- confirmed via coordinates that this entry is the correct Poum-area site McFadyen dived, not the Bourail site.
